name: Fire Inspection Checklist
description: A fire-safety inspection of a building or workplace covering equipment, exits and hazards.

items.text: Confirm extinguishers are present, charged and within their service date.
Check the pressure gauge, pin and tamper seal on each unit.
Verify extinguishers are mounted, signed and unobstructed.
items.note: Note the inspection tag date for each extinguisher.

items.text: Confirm fire blankets and hose reels, where fitted, are accessible.
Check that monthly and annual inspection records are current.
Walk every exit route and confirm it is clear and unobstructed.
Check exit doors open freely and are not locked or blocked.
Confirm fire doors close and latch and are not propped open.
Verify exit and directional signs are visible and illuminated.
items.note: Report any propped fire door or failed exit sign immediately.

items.text: Test emergency and backup lighting along escape routes.
Confirm stairwells are clear and self-closing doors function.
Confirm smoke and heat detectors are in place and not painted over.
Verify the fire alarm panel shows no faults and is monitored.
Test that alarm signals are audible and visible throughout.
Check manual call points are accessible and unobstructed.
Confirm the last alarm service and test dates are recorded.
Confirm sprinkler heads are unobstructed and undamaged.
Verify at least the required clearance below each sprinkler head.
items.note: Keep storage well below sprinkler heads to maintain coverage.

items.text: Check control valves are open, accessible and supervised.
Confirm kitchen or specialty suppression systems are serviced.
Verify the last sprinkler inspection and service dates are recorded.
Check electrical panels are accessible with required clearance.
Inspect wiring, cords and sockets for damage or overloading.
Confirm flammable liquids are stored in approved cabinets.
Verify combustible waste and materials are kept away from ignition sources.
Check that aisles, exits and equipment access remain clear.
Record the date, inspector and areas covered.
Document each deficiency with a clear location and description.
Assign corrective actions with owners and target dates.
Track deficiencies to closure and verify completed repairs.
Confirm inspection records are retained and accessible.

Important: this is general guidance only and does not replace OSHA regulations, local fire codes, formal training or inspection by a qualified person or the authority having jurisdiction; confirm requirements for your building.

faq.q: How is a fire inspection different from a fire safety program?
faq.a: A fire safety program sets prevention rules, training and procedures, while a fire inspection is a point-in-time walkthrough that verifies the building physically meets those requirements and documents any deficiencies for correction.

faq.q: How often should a building fire inspection be done?
faq.a: Conduct internal inspections at least monthly for extinguishers and quarterly for a broader walk, with annual professional servicing of alarms, sprinklers and suppression systems. Your local fire code may require specific intervals.

faq.q: What are common fire inspection failures?
faq.a: Frequent findings include blocked or locked exits, obstructed extinguishers or sprinkler heads, expired equipment, failed emergency lighting, propped fire doors and improperly stored combustibles or flammable liquids.

faq.q: Who can carry out a fire inspection?
faq.a: Trained facility staff or safety officers can run routine internal inspections, while the authority having jurisdiction conducts official inspections. Alarm and sprinkler systems generally require servicing by qualified contractors.

faq.q: Does this checklist replace an official inspection?
faq.a: No. It is general guidance and does not replace OSHA regulations, local fire codes, formal training, your employer's fire program, or inspection by a qualified person or the authority having jurisdiction. Always confirm the rules for your building.
